articles.title: Ötzi the Iceman's 5,300-Year-Old Microbes Are Still Alive—and That's a Problem
articles.summary: Four species of yeast found on Ötzi the Iceman can grow in a lab, proving they survived millennia in ice. These dormant microbes could decompose the mummy. Researchers are studying them to protect this priceless archaeological find.

articles.title: How the Universe Outruns Light Without Breaking Physics
articles.summary: The observable universe spans 45 billion light-years despite being 13.77 billion years old. Cosmic expansion, driven by dark energy, allows space to stretch faster than light—without violating relativity. The cosmological event horizon limits what we'll ever see.

articles.title: Inside the 1997 Mir Collision: Astronaut Michael Foale on a Near-Death Crisis in Space
articles.summary: In a new interview, astronaut Michael Foale recounts the 1997 Mir space station collision, when a Progress cargo ship crashed into the station, causing decompression. With 23 minutes of oxygen left, the crew's heroics saved the station. Foale reveals the cost-cutting that led to the disaster.
